question:
The points $A(1,2)$, $B(4,6)$, and $C(k,10)$ form a triangle.

(a) Determine the value of $k$ for which the three points are collinear.

(b) Find the values of $k$ for which the area of $\triangle ABC$ is $6$ square units.

(c) Examine whether the collinear value obtained in part (a) lies between the two values obtained in part (b).
explanation:
(a)
For three points to be collinear, the determinant representing twice their area must be zero:
$$\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2 & 1\\4 & 6 & 1\\k & 10 & 1\end{vmatrix}=0$$
Expanding,
$$1(6-10)-2(4-k)+(40-6k)=0$$
$$-4-8+2k+40-6k=0$$
$$28-4k=0$$
Therefore,
$$k=7$$

(b)
The area of the triangle is
$$\text{Area}=\frac{1}{2}|28-4k|$$
Given that the area is $6$ square units,
$$\frac{1}{2}|28-4k|=6$$
$$|28-4k|=12$$
Thus,
$$28-4k=12\quad\text{or}\quad28-4k=-12$$
Hence,
$$k=4\quad\text{or}\quad k=10$$

(c)
The values obtained in part (b) are $4$ and $10$. Since
$$4<7<10$$
the collinear value $k=7$ lies between the two values for which the area is $6$ square units.

options.A:
(a) The points are collinear when $k=7$
(b) The area is $6$ square units when $k=4$ or $k=10$
(c) Yes, $4<7<10$
options.B:
(a) The points are collinear when $k=6$
(b) The area is $6$ square units when $k=3$ or $k=9$
(c) Yes, the collinear value lies between them
options.C:
(a) The points are collinear when $k=7$
(b) The area is $6$ square units when $k=5$ or $k=9$
(c) Yes, $5<7<9$
options.D:
(a) The points are collinear when $k=7$
(b) The area is $6$ square units when $k=4$ or $k=10$
(c) No, $k=7$ does not lie between the two values
